plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Silvery-green mounds send up slender spikes of fragrant violet-blue flowers. Fields of lavender hum with bees and release a sweet, herbal perfume in the summer heat.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late summer, peaking from late June through July to early August
plants.location: Provence, southern France, and Mediterranean Europe
plants.funFact: The name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'. Romans scented their baths with lavender.

plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: Tall, sturdy stems carry huge golden-rayed flower heads that look like small suns. Young flower heads follow the sun's path across the sky, and whole fields glow in midsummer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn, with many fields opening from July
plants.location: Central and northern Europe and the North American Great Plains
plants.funFact: Each sunflower head is made up of hundreds to thousands of tiny individual flowers. Their seeds are arranged in spirals that follow the Fibonacci sequence.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: Large, cup-shaped blossoms rise on tall stalks above round, water-repellent leaves. They open at dawn on still ponds and lakes, and they are among the most striking sights of the monsoon and summer months.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer, roughly June to September, across its temperate and subtropical range
plants.location: Ponds and wetlands across Asia, including India, China and Japan
plants.funFact: Lotus leaves have a microscopic surface texture that makes water bead up and roll off, taking dirt with it. Scientists call this the 'lotus effect' and have copied it in self-cleaning materials.
